Neck Pain & Headaches Physiotherapy in Brookvale
Neck pain, stiffness and headaches can affect your ability to work, sleep, exercise and enjoy everyday activities.
Some headaches originate from the neck and can be associated with neck stiffness, restricted movement or muscle tension.
We assess your symptoms to understand what may be contributing to your pain and develop a treatment plan to help you move comfortably again.
What is neck pain?
(the what is neck pain / headaches and common symptoms to have the same layout as back pain & sciatica)
note: What is / symptoms sections use the Lower back pain and Sciatica layout

text: Neck pain refers to discomfort, stiffness or restricted movement in the area between the base of your skull and the top of your shoulders.
It can develop gradually or acutely and affects people of all ages and activity levels.
Neck pain can be influenced by a range of factors, including muscle and joint sensitivity, prolonged positions, physical activity, stress and previous injuries.
Symptoms can also spread into the shoulders, upper back or arms.
What are neck-related headaches?
Some headaches originate from structures in the neck, known as cervicogenic headaches.
They can occur when joints and muscles in the neck contribute to pain that is felt in the head.
These headaches are often associated with neck pain or stiffness and may be aggravated by certain neck movements or sustained positions.
A physiotherapy assessment can help determine whether the neck may be contributing to your headaches and whether treatment is appropriate.
Common symptoms
Neck pain
Aching, stiffness or tightness through the neck and top of your shoulders.
Pain or difficulty turning your head or looking up and down.
Muscle tension or discomfort around the base of the skull.
Pain spreading into the shoulders, upper back or arms.
Neck-related headaches
Headaches starting around the base of the skull or back of the head.
Pain that can spread towards the forehead, temples or behind the eyes.
Headaches associated with neck stiffness or restricted movement.
Headaches aggravated by certain neck movements or sustained positions.
Headaches that occur alongside neck or shoulder discomfort.
What causes neck pain & headaches?
Prolonged positions
Spending long periods sitting at a desk, driving or looking down at devices can contribute to neck pain, particularly when movement is limited throughout the day.
Muscle strength and endurance
Reduced strength or endurance through the neck, shoulders and upper back can affect how your body manages everyday activities.
Joint and muscle sensitivity
The joints, muscles and surrounding structures of the neck can become sensitive, contributing to pain, stiffness and restricted movement.
In some cases, these structures can also contribute to headaches.
Previous injuries
Previous neck injuries, including whiplash, can sometimes lead to ongoing pain, stiffness or reduced movement.
Sleep, stress and general health
Poor sleep, stress and increased physical or mental demands can influence muscle tension, pain sensitivity and recovery.
How we assess and treat neck pain & headaches
Assessment
We discuss your symptoms, daily activities and goals, then assess your neck movement, mobility and strength.
We also assess your shoulders and upper back to understand what may be contributing to your symptoms.
Manage symptoms
Hands-on treatment, targeted exercises and practical advice help reduce pain, improve movement and manage muscle and joint sensitivity.
Build strength and mobility
Progressive exercises for your neck, shoulders and upper back help restore movement, improve strength and build tolerance for everyday activities, work and exercise.
What to expect from neck pain & headache physiotherapy
Headaches?
Not all headaches originate from the neck.
We'll assess whether that's the case and help guide you towards appropriate care if further medical investigation is needed.
Posture?
You don't need to maintain one perfect posture all day.
We'll help you find ways to manage prolonged positions, vary your movement and build tolerance for everyday activities.
Time frame?
Recovery varies depending on the cause, severity and duration of your symptoms.
Some people improve within a few weeks, while persistent or recurring symptoms may benefit from a longer rehabilitation plan.
At home
You'll leave with practical advice and exercises to help manage your symptoms, including guidance around movement, desk work, sleep and everyday activities.
When to see a GP or seek urgent care
A sudden, severe headache that reaches maximum intensity within seconds or minutes.
A new or unusual headache accompanied by vision changes, confusion, difficulty speaking, weakness or loss of coordination.
Neck pain or headache accompanied by fever, a rash or feeling very unwell.
New or worsening numbness, tingling or weakness in the arms or hands.
Neck pain or headache following a significant accident or injury.
A new, persistent or progressively worsening headache, particularly if it is different from your usual headaches.
A sudden severe headache or headache accompanied by new neurological symptoms requires emergency assessment.
Call 000 or attend an emergency department.
Shoulder & Arm Pain Physiotherapy in Brookvale
Shoulder and arm pain can affect everything from lifting and reaching to working, exercising and everyday activities.
From rotator cuff injuries and frozen shoulder to tennis elbow and tendon problems, we assess and treat a wide range of conditions to help reduce pain, restore movement and rebuild strength.
Shoulder & Arm Conditions We See
Shoulder and arm pain can develop gradually through repetitive activities and loading, or occur suddenly following an injury.
Symptoms can affect the shoulder, upper arm, elbow and forearm, sometimes making everyday movements uncomfortable or difficult.

Whether you're struggling to lift your arm, experiencing pain during gym training or dealing with persistent elbow pain, we tailor treatment and rehabilitation to your symptoms, activity levels and goals.
Common Shoulder & Arm Conditions
Rotator cuff tears and injuries
Shoulder bursitis and tendon pain
Shoulder ‘impingement’
Frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis)
Shoulder instability and dislocations
AC joint injuries
Tennis elbow (lateral epicondylalgia)
Golfer's elbow (medial epicondylalgia)
Shoulder and arm pain following fractures or surgery
What Contributes to Shoulder & Arm Pain?
Repetitive Activities and Loading
Repeated lifting, reaching, overhead activities and gripping can place increased demands on the shoulder, elbow and surrounding tendons.
Strength and Movement Control
Reduced strength, endurance or movement control around the shoulder blade, rotator cuff and arm can affect how the shoulder and arm manage everyday and sporting activities.
Sudden Injury or Overload
Falls, lifting heavy objects, or sudden increases in your gym training or activity can result in muscle strains or tendon injuries.
Work and Lifestyle Demands
Repetitive manual work, prolonged computer use and activities involving sustained or repeated arm movements can contribute to ongoing symptoms.
Previous Injuries and Age-Related Changes
Previous shoulder or arm injuries, as well as changes in tendons and joints over time, can influence strength, mobility and how well the area tolerates physical demands.
How We Assess and Treat Shoulder & Arm Pain
Assessment
We discuss your history, symptoms, daily activities and goals, then assess your shoulder and arm movement, mobility and strength.
We'll also assess and identify other factors that may be contributing to your symptoms.
Manage Symptoms
Hands-on treatment, targeted exercises and practical advice help reduce pain, improve movement and restore function.
We'll also guide you on modifying activities where needed while symptoms settle.
Build Strength and Restore Function
Progressive strengthening and rehabilitation help improve shoulder stability, tendon capacity and arm function.
Exercises are tailored to your needs, whether that's returning to the gym, playing sport or managing everyday activities comfortably.
What to Expect from Shoulder & Arm Physiotherapy
Scans?
Most conditions can initially be assessed through a clinical examination without requiring imaging.
If further investigation is needed, we'll guide you on whether an X-ray, ultrasound or MRI may be appropriate.
Movement?
Keeping the shoulder and arm moving within comfortable limits is generally encouraged.
We'll help you understand which movements and activities to modify and how to gradually restore your movement.
Time Frame?
Recovery varies depending on the condition, severity and duration of symptoms.
Some problems improve over several months, while others require longer rehabilitation.
At Home
You'll leave with practical advice and exercises to help manage your symptoms, maintain movement and build strength between appointments.
When to See a GP or Seek Urgent Care
Sudden severe shoulder pain following an injury, particularly if you cannot move your arm.
An obvious shoulder deformity or suspected dislocation.
Significant swelling or bruising following an injury.
New or worsening numbness, tingling or weakness in the arm or hand.
A hot, red or swollen shoulder accompanied by fever or feeling unwell.
Shoulder or arm pain accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, nausea or dizziness.
Shoulder or arm pain accompanied by chest pain, breathlessness or other possible cardiac symptoms requires emergency assessment.
Call 000.
Hip & Groin Pain Physiotherapy in Brookvale
Hip and groin pain can affect walking, running, exercise and everyday activities.

From hip bursitis and gluteal tendinopathy to groin strains and hip joint problems, we assess and treat a wide range of conditions to help reduce pain, restore movement and improve strength and function.
Hip & Groin Conditions We Treat
Hip and groin pain can develop gradually through repetitive loading and activity, or occur suddenly following an injury.
Symptoms may affect the hip joint, surrounding muscles and tendons, or the groin and inner thigh, sometimes making walking, running and everyday movements uncomfortable.
Whether you're experiencing pain when walking, struggling with gym exercises or developing groin pain during sport, we tailor treatment and rehabilitation to your symptoms, activity levels and goals.
Common Hip & Groin Conditions
Gluteal tendinopathy
Hip bursitis
Hip osteoarthritis
Hip impingement and labral injuries
Hip flexor, adductor and hamstring strains and tendinopathy
Hip pain following surgery or joint replacement
What Contributes to Hip & Groin Pain?
Changes in Activity and Training Load
Sudden increases in walking, running, gym training or sporting activity can place greater demands on the hip and surrounding muscles and tendons.
Strength and Movement Control
Reduced strength or endurance through the hips, glutes and surrounding muscles can affect how your body manages everyday activities, running and sport.
Repetitive Movements and Loading
Activities involving repeated running, kicking, twisting or changes of direction can place increased demands on the hip and groin, particularly when training loads increase quickly.
Joint and Tendon Changes
Changes within the hip joint, including osteoarthritis, labral injuries and joint variations, can contribute to pain and restricted movement.
Tendons and surrounding soft tissues can also become sensitive with repetitive loading.
Previous Injuries and Recovery
Previous hip, groin or hamstring injuries, particularly where strength and function have not been fully restored, can affect your ability to tolerate physical activity.
How We Assess and Treat Hip & Groin Pain
Assessment
We discuss your symptoms, injury history, daily activities and goals, then assess your hip movement, mobility, strength and surrounding structures to understand what may be contributing to your pain.
Manage Symptoms
Hands-on treatment, targeted exercises and practical advice help reduce pain, improve movement and manage symptoms.
We'll also guide you on modifying activities where needed while symptoms settle.
Build Strength and Restore Function
Progressive strengthening for the hips, glutes and surrounding muscles helps improve stability, restore function and build tolerance for everyday activities, work, running and sport.
What to Expect from Hip & Groin Physiotherapy
Scans?
Most hip and groin conditions can initially be assessed through a clinical examination without requiring imaging.
If further investigation is needed, we'll guide you on what may be appropriate for you.
Movement?
Keeping active within comfortable limits is generally encouraged.
We'll help you understand which activities and movements to modify and how to gradually rebuild your strength and movement.
Time Frame?
Recovery varies depending on the condition, severity and duration of symptoms.
Muscle strains may settle over several weeks, while tendon and joint-related conditions can require a longer rehabilitation plan.
At Home
You'll leave with practical advice and exercises to help manage your symptoms, maintain movement and build strength between appointments.
When to See a GP or Seek Urgent Care
Inability to weight-bear or walk following a sudden injury.
Significant pain following a fall or accident.
Severe hip or groin pain accompanied by fever or feeling very unwell.
New numbness or weakness in the legs, or changes to bladder or bowel control.
A painful groin or hip lump, particularly if accompanied by severe abdominal pain, vomiting or feeling unwell.
Sudden severe hip or groin pain with an inability to weight-bear, particularly following an injury, requires urgent medical assessment.
Knee Pain & Injury Physiotherapy in Brookvale
Knee pain can affect walking, running, climbing stairs, exercising and everyday activities.
From meniscus and ligament injuries to knee osteoarthritis and tendon problems, we assess and treat a wide range of knee conditions.
Knee Conditions We Treat
Knee pain can develop suddenly following an injury, such as a ligament sprain or meniscus tear, or gradually through repetitive loading and changes in activity.
Symptoms can affect people of all ages and activity levels, from those experiencing everyday knee stiffness to athletes returning from sporting injuries.

Whether you're struggling with knee pain when walking, experiencing discomfort during exercise or recovering from a sporting injury or surgery, we tailor treatment and rehabilitation to your symptoms, activity levels and goals.
Common Knee Conditions
Knee osteoarthritis
Patellofemoral pain (runner's knee)
Meniscus injuries and tears
ACL, MCL and other knee ligament injuries
Patellar tendinopathy (jumper's knee)
ITB-related knee pain
Knee bursitis
Quadriceps and hamstring strains
Patella (kneecap) dislocations and instability
Following surgery, such as ACL reconstruction and knee replacement
What Contributes to Knee Pain?
Changes in Activity and Training Load
Sudden increases in walking, running, gym training or sporting activity can place greater demands on the knee, potentially contributing to pain and irritation.
Strength and Movement Control
Reduced strength or endurance through the quadriceps, hamstrings and glutes can affect how your body manages everyday movements and sporting activities.
Repetitive Loading
Activities involving repeated running, jumping, squatting and climbing stairs can place increased demands on the knee, particularly when training loads increase too quickly.
Joint and Soft Tissue Changes
Changes within the knee joint, including osteoarthritis and meniscus injuries, can contribute to pain, swelling and restricted movement.
Tendons, ligaments and surrounding soft tissues can also become injured or sensitive.
Previous Injuries and Recovery
Previous knee injuries, particularly where strength, stability and function have not been fully restored, can increase the risk of ongoing symptoms or further injury.
How We Assess and Treat Knee Pain
Assessment
We discuss your symptoms, injury history, daily activities and goals, then assess your lower limb movement, strength and stability to understand what may be contributing to your pain.
Manage Symptoms
Hands-on treatment, targeted exercises and practical advice help reduce pain, manage swelling, improve movement and restore function.
We'll also guide you on modifying activities where needed while symptoms settle.
Build Strength and Restore Function
Progressive strengthening for the quadriceps, hamstrings, hips and surrounding muscles helps improve knee stability, restore function and build tolerance for everyday activities, running and sport.
What to Expect from Knee Physiotherapy
Scans?
Most knee conditions do not require imaging.
If further investigation is needed, we'll guide you on whether an X-ray, ultrasound or MRI may be appropriate.
Movement?
Keeping active within comfortable limits is generally encouraged.
We'll help you understand which activities to modify and how to gradually restore your movement and strength.
Time Frame?
Recovery varies depending on the condition, severity and duration of symptoms.
Minor injuries may improve over several weeks, while ligament injuries, tendon problems and post-surgical rehabilitation can require a longer recovery plan.
At Home
You'll leave with practical advice and exercises to help manage your symptoms, maintain movement and build strength between appointments.
When to See a GP or Seek Urgent Care
Inability to weight-bear following a sudden injury.
Significant swelling that develops quickly after an injury.
An obvious knee deformity or suspected dislocation.
A knee that becomes locked and cannot fully straighten.
A hot, red or swollen knee accompanied by fever or feeling very unwell.
New or worsening calf swelling, pain or tenderness, particularly following surgery or prolonged immobility.
Sudden significant knee swelling, deformity or inability to weight-bear following an injury warrants urgent medical assessment.
Foot & Ankle Physiotherapy in Brookvale
Ankle and foot pain can affect walking, running, exercise and everyday activities.
From ankle sprains to shin splints, we assess and treat a wide range of conditions to help reduce pain, restore movement and rebuild strength and function.
We also work alongside The Foot Company's podiatrist when foot-related concerns require a combined approach to care.
Foot & Ankle Conditions We Treat
Foot and ankle pain can develop suddenly following an injury, such as an ankle sprain or fracture, or gradually through repetitive loading and changes in activity.
Symptoms can affect the ankle, heel and lower leg, sometimes making walking, running and everyday movements uncomfortable.

Whether you're recovering from an ankle injury, experiencing recurring ankle sprains or developing pain during running and exercise, we tailor treatment and rehabilitation to your symptoms, activity levels and goals.
Common Foot & Ankle Conditions
Ankle sprains and ligament injuries
Chronic ankle instability
Achilles tendinopathy
Plantar heel pain (plantar fasciitis)
Peroneal tendinopathy
Stress fractures and bone stress injuries
Shin splints (medial tibial stress syndrome)
Calf strains and lower leg injuries
Foot and ankle rehabilitation following fractures or surgery
What Contributes to Foot & Ankle Pain?
Changes in Activity and Training Load
Sudden increases in walking, running, jumping or sporting activity can place greater demands on the foot and ankle, potentially contributing to pain and irritation.
Strength and Movement Control
Reduced strength, balance or stability through the feet, ankles and lower legs can affect how your body manages everyday activities and sporting movements.
Repetitive Loading
Activities involving prolonged walking, running and jumping place repeated demands on the feet and ankles.
When these demands exceed the body's ability to adapt, pain and tendon problems can develop.
Previous Injuries
Previous ankle sprains or foot and ankle injuries, particularly where strength, balance and stability have not been fully restored, can increase the risk of ongoing symptoms or further injury.
Foot Mechanics and Loading
Differences in foot structure, movement and loading can influence how forces are distributed through the lower limb.
In some cases, assessment and management from both physiotherapy and podiatry can help address these contributing factors.
How We Assess and Treat Foot & Ankle Pain
Assessment
We discuss your symptoms, injury history, daily activities and goals, then assess your lower limb movement, strength, balance and stability to understand what may be contributing to your pain.
Manage Symptoms
Hands-on treatment, targeted exercises and practical advice help reduce pain, manage swelling, improve movement and restore function.
We'll also guide you on modifying activities where needed while symptoms settle.
Build Strength and Restore Function
Progressive strengthening, balance and rehabilitation exercises help improve ankle stability, restore function and build tolerance for everyday activities, walking, running and sport.
Working Alongside Podiatry

Our physiotherapy team works alongside The Foot Company's podiatrist, allowing us to take a collaborative approach when foot mechanics, footwear or other foot-related factors may be contributing to your symptoms.
Where appropriate, we can coordinate care or refer you for a podiatry assessment to complement your physiotherapy treatment.
What to Expect from Foot & Ankle Physiotherapy
Scans?
Most foot and ankle conditions can initially be assessed through a clinical examination without requiring imaging.
If further investigation is needed, we'll guide you on what may be appropriate.
Movement?
Keeping active within comfortable limits is generally encouraged.
We'll help you understand which activities to modify and how to gradually restore your movement, strength and walking or running capacity.
Time Frame?
Recovery varies depending on the condition, severity and duration of symptoms.
Minor ankle sprains may improve over several weeks, while tendon problems, stress injuries and recurring ankle instability can require a longer rehabilitation plan.
At Home
You'll leave with practical advice and exercises to help manage your symptoms, maintain movement and build strength and stability between appointments.
When to See a GP or Seek Urgent Care
Inability to weight-bear or walk following an injury.
Significant swelling, bruising or deformity following a fall or accident.
A sudden popping sensation in the Achilles tendon, particularly with difficulty pushing off or standing on your toes.
A hot, red or swollen foot or ankle accompanied by fever or feeling very unwell.
New numbness, loss of sensation or changes in foot colour or temperature.
Inability to weight-bear following an injury, suspected fracture or sudden loss of Achilles function warrants prompt medical assessment.
Adolescent Sports Injuries & Physiotherapy in Brookvale
Adolescence is a time of rapid growth and physical development, which can place additional demands on muscles, tendons and developing bones.
We treat a range of conditions affecting active children and teenagers.
Our aim is to manage pain, support healthy development and help young athletes stay active and return to sport safely.
Adolescent Injuries We Treat
During growth spurts, bones can grow faster than surrounding muscles and tendons adapt, sometimes contributing to tightness, pain and increased sensitivity around growth plates.
Combined with the demands of training and sport, this can make adolescents more susceptible to certain injuries.

Whether your child is experiencing knee or heel pain during sport, struggling with recurring injuries or recovering from a sporting injury, we tailor treatment and rehabilitation to their stage of development, activity levels and sporting goals.
Common Adolescent Injuries
Osgood-Schlatter disease (traction apophysitis of the knee)
Sever's disease (traction apophysitis of the heel)
Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome (traction apophysitis of the kneecap)
Hip and pelvic apophysitis
Growth-related heel, knee and hip pain
Muscle strains, including hamstring, calf and groin injuries
Ankle sprains and ligament injuries
Knee ligament and meniscus injuries
Patellofemoral pain (kneecap-related pain)
Bone stress injuries
What Contributes to Adolescent Injuries?
Growth and Development
During growth spurts, bones can grow faster than muscles and tendons adapt.
This can increase tension around growth plates and attachment sites, contributing to conditions such as Osgood-Schlatter and Sever's disease.
Changes in Training Load
Sudden increases in training frequency, intensity or sporting commitments can place greater demands on a developing body, particularly when recovery is limited.
Strength and Muscle Flexibility
Changes in muscle length, strength and flexibility during growth can affect how the body manages sporting movements and physical demands.
Repetitive Loading
Sports involving repeated running, jumping, kicking and changes of direction can place significant demands on developing bones, joints and tendons.
How We Assess and Treat Adolescent Injuries
Assessment
We discuss your child's symptoms, sporting activities, training schedule and goals, then assess their movement, strength and function to understand what may be contributing to their pain.
Manage Symptoms
Treatment focuses on managing pain, modifying activity where needed and maintaining appropriate movement and strength while symptoms settle.
We'll provide guidance around training adjustments and when it is appropriate to continue or temporarily modify activity.
Build Strength and Return to Sport
Progressive strengthening, balance and sport-specific exercises help restore function and build tolerance for training and competition.
Rehabilitation is tailored to your child's development, sporting demands and goals, with a gradual return to sport when appropriate.
What to Expect from Adolescent Sports Physiotherapy
Keep Playing?
Not every injury requires stopping sport completely.
We'll help determine which activities can continue, what may need modifying and when a temporary break from certain activities is appropriate.
Growth and Development?
Some conditions, particularly traction apophysitis, are related to growth and may fluctuate during periods of rapid development.
We'll help manage symptoms while maintaining appropriate strength and activity.
Time Frame?
Some conditions settle over several weeks, while growth-related injuries can require ongoing management as the body develops.
At Home
You'll receive practical advice and exercises to help manage symptoms, maintain strength and support recovery between appointments.
We'll also provide guidance for parents and young athletes around training loads and return to sport.
When to See a GP or Seek Urgent Care
Inability to weight-bear or walk following an injury.
Significant swelling or an obvious deformity following a fall or sporting injury.
Severe or worsening pain, particularly pain that occurs at rest or wakes your child at night.
A hot, red or swollen joint accompanied by fever or feeling very unwell.
Persistent or worsening bone pain, particularly pain that is becoming more localised or occurs with progressively less activity.
Significant pain following an injury with loss of movement or function.
Persistent or worsening pain should be medically assessed rather than assumed to be a normal part of growing.
Sudden severe pain, suspected fracture or inability to weight-bear following an injury warrants urgent medical assessment.

text: Exercise for Osteoporosis in Brookvale
Physiotherapy and exercise programs for osteoporosis in Brookvale.
We develop individualised exercise programs to build strength, improve balance and support bone health, while guiding you on which movements may need to be modified.
Osteoporosis and Exercise
Osteoporosis is a condition where bones become less dense and more fragile, increasing the risk of fractures, particularly in the hips, spine and wrists.
Osteopenia refers to lower-than-normal bone density, but not as low as osteoporosis.
Both are common, particularly as we age and in women following menopause.
There is generally no obvious symptoms until a fracture occurs.
Exercise is an important part of managing osteoporosis.
Progressive strength training, weight-bearing exercise and balance training help support bone health, maintain muscle strength and reduce the risk of falls.
Your physiotherapist will also guide you on movements that may need to be modified, particularly heavily loaded forward bending and twisting, depending on your bone health and fracture history.
Exercise for Osteoporosis May Suit You If
You've been diagnosed with osteoporosis or osteopenia.
You've had a fracture following a minor fall or everyday activity.
You want to exercise but are unsure which movements are safe.
You feel less steady on your feet than you used to.
You want to maintain strength, mobility and independence as you get older.
Exercise for Osteoporosis: What a Program Includes
Programs are tailored to your bone density, fracture history, fitness, physical abilities and individual goals.
Strength Training
Progressive resistance exercises to build muscle strength and place appropriate loading through the bones.
Weight-Bearing Exercise
Activities such as walking and, where appropriate, low-level impact exercise to support bone health.
Balance Training
Exercises to improve balance, coordination and confidence with movement, helping reduce the risk of falls.
Posture and Spine Care
Strengthening the back extensor muscles and learning how to bend, lift and move safely.
How We Assess and Plan Exercise for Osteoporosis
Physiotherapy Assessment
We review your medical history, bone density results and fracture history, then assess your strength, balance, posture and physical function to guide your exercise program.
Individualised Exercise Program
A combination of progressive strength, balance and posture exercises based on your assessment, with clear guidance on movements that may need to be modified.
Ongoing Exercise and Progression
Continue with one on one sessions, clinical pilates, or our small Active Seniors classes, with exercises progressed to support your strength, balance and independence.
When to See a GP or Seek Urgent Care
Sudden or severe back pain following a minor strain, cough or lifting activity, which may indicate a spinal fracture.
Noticeable loss of height or a new change in posture, such as increased rounding of the upper back.
A fall followed by significant pain, swelling or difficulty moving or weight-bearing.
You have been diagnosed with osteoporosis but haven't had your bone health or fracture risk reviewed by your GP.
Suspected fractures require medical assessment before continuing or starting exercise.
Sudden severe back pain or suspected spinal or hip fracture warrants prompt medical attention.
In an emergency, call 000.

text: NDIS Physiotherapy in Brookvale
We provide physiotherapy for NDIS participants, helping improve strength, mobility, balance and physical function to support greater independence and participation in everyday activities.
WHO IT IS FOR
Physiotherapy built around your goals
Whether you're looking to improve your mobility, manage an ongoing condition, build strength or maintain your independence, we tailor physiotherapy to your individual needs, abilities and goals.
We welcome self-managed and plan-managed NDIS participants at our Brookvale and Terrey Hills clinics.
This may suit you if
You're an NDIS participant with self-managed or plan-managed funding.
You want to improve your strength, mobility or balance.
You need support managing a physical condition or injury.
You want to maintain your independence and everyday function.
You have specific physical goals you'd like to work towards.
WHAT WE HELP WITH:
Tap a topic to see how physiotherapy may help.
Mobility and movement
Improving walking, movement and physical ability for everyday activities.
Strength and conditioning
Building strength, endurance and physical capacity to support daily activities and independence.
Balance and falls prevention
Improving balance, coordination and confidence with movement to help reduce falls risk.
Pain and injury management
Managing musculoskeletal pain, injuries and physical limitations that affect everyday function.
Long-term conditions
Supporting people living with ongoing physical conditions to maintain or improve strength, mobility and function.
What to expect:
What will physiotherapy look like?
Assessment and goal setting
We discuss your medical history, current abilities, daily activities and NDIS goals, followed by an assessment of your movement, strength, balance and physical function.
Treatment and rehabilitation
Hands-on treatment where appropriate, combined with an individualised exercise and rehabilitation program to improve movement, manage symptoms and build physical capacity.
Progress and ongoing support
Your rehabilitation is adjusted as you progress, with exercises and practical strategies to help you work towards your goals and maintain improvements between appointments.
Your first appointment
What happens
We'll discuss your medical history, current needs, everyday activities and goals, followed by an assessment of your movement, strength, balance and physical function.
How long
Your first appointment is 60 minutes at Brookvale and 45 minutes at Terrey Hills.
Follow-up appointments are 30 minutes.
What to bring
Your NDIS plan or relevant plan details, information about your goals and funding arrangements, a list of medications and any relevant medical reports or imaging results.
Why solevo:
Physiotherapy focused on your goals and independence
01 – Individualised treatment
Physiotherapy tailored to your abilities, support needs and individual goals.
02 – Strength and functional rehabilitation
Build strength, balance and physical capacity to support everyday activities and greater independence.
Our Brookvale clinic has a dedicated rehabilitation space with strength training equipment.
03 – Working towards your goals
We monitor your progress and adjust your rehabilitation to support your goals and changing needs.
Where appropriate, we can communicate with your support coordinator, plan manager, treating doctor and other members of your support team.

We cannot provide NDIS-funded services to NDIA-managed participants.

Plan-managed participants can arrange payment through their plan manager, while self-managed participants can pay for appointments and claim reimbursement through the NDIS.

text: Active Seniors Exercise Program in Brookvale
Physiotherapist-led seniors exercise classes in Brookvale, focused on building strength, improving balance, bone health and maintaining mobility and independence.
Our small group classes run on Mondays and Fridays, with a one-to-one physiotherapy assessment before you begin to ensure exercises are suited to your needs and abilities.
What the Classes Cover
Our Active Seniors classes focus on building strength, improving balance and maintaining the mobility needed for everyday life.
Exercises include functional strength training, balance activities and mobility work, all guided by a physiotherapist and adapted to suit your individual ability.
Before joining, you'll have a one-on-one assessment with a physiotherapist.
We'll discuss your health, medical history, any previous falls, joint concerns and bone health, then assess your strength, balance and mobility.
This helps us tailor exercises to your needs and identify any modifications before your first class.
Who the Active Seniors Program Is For
Feeling less steady on your feet or concerned about falling.
Wanting to maintain or improve strength, balance and mobility.
Osteoporosis or osteopenia, and looking for appropriate exercise.
Arthritis, stiff joints or a previous joint replacement.
New to exercise or returning after a break.
Wanting to maintain independence and keep up with family, travel and hobbies.
What Our Active Seniors Classes Focus On
01 – Better Balance
Exercises that challenge and improve balance, coordination and stability, helping build confidence when walking and moving around and reduce the risk of falls.
02 – Strength for Everyday Life
Progressive strength exercises targeting the legs, hips, back and core to support everyday activities such as climbing stairs, getting up from a chair and carrying shopping.
03 – Bone Health
